main_text.p: quidem, qua verbum verbo iuxta ordinem Grammaticum redditur. Altera verò qua verfibus Latinis verfus Italici respondent: vti facilius ex ipsa libelli lectione id cognosci poterit. Quàm autem utilis & necessaria sit Viro Nobili linguarum cognitio, non Latinæ & Græcæ tantùm, quæ eruditorum linguæ sunt, quibus liberales artes & disciplinæ traduntur; sed vernacularum etiam, superfedeo dicere, ne actum agere videar: abundè enim id ex splendida eáque pererudita de Viro nobili oratione illa, cognoscere potuisti. De linguæ autem Italicæ præstantia, dignitate, suauitate, aliisque virtutibus, quibus fortasse & Gallicam & Hispanicam antecellit, nolo nunc dicere, quod odiosum omnino argum

page.notes: The running head reads "EPISTOLA." and is printed in spaced capitals. The last line "gum" is a fragment of the catchword-like word "argumentum" split at the page foot; it is printed right-aligned at the foot of the text and is transcribed as "gum" in the text above. The reading "superfedeo" and "ne actum" are as printed; "vernacularum etiam,superfedeo" has a missing word between "etiam" and "superfedeo" as printed. The word "odiosum" and "omnino" are as printed.
